references.text: Eleazar the priest gives a similar regulation concerning 'the statute of the law' (חֻקַּת הַתּוֹרָה), which refers to purification rituals.
A heifer that has never borne a yoke is used in the ritual for an unsolved murder, the same requirement as for the red heifer.
The requirement that the sacrificial animal must be without blemish (תְּמִימָה אֲשֶׁר אֵין־בָּהּ מוּם) is repeated here for all sacrifices.
Cows that have never borne a yoke are used to carry the ark of the covenant, corresponding to the requirement for the red heifer.
The Letter to the Hebrews refers directly to the ashes of the red heifer and their cleansing power, comparing this with Christ's blood that cleanses the conscience.
Christ as a lamb without blemish or spot (ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου) fulfills the requirement for a flawless sacrifice.
The sin offering requires a young bull without blemish (תָּמִים), the same basic requirement of flawlessness.
